ledger.contains: 2024 Budget Address (13 Dec 2023, 62 pages). Programme content: the first CBI dividend (paid for the first time in the programme's history; about 17,500 people reached in its inaugural round; paid to Social Security contributors); 2022 non-tax revenue 54.9% above budget mainly because of CBI proceeds (no CBI amount); CBI section (paras 51-53): real estate option minimum US$400,000, mandatory applicant interviews and the Sustainable Island State Contribution introduced, enhanced due diligence; medium-term plan to reduce reliance on CBI revenue and to explore saving part of it in a dedicated fund. No CBI revenue amount is printed. The rest (macro outlook, sector policies, debt, social programmes, worker bonus) is out of scope.

2025 Budget Address (16 Dec 2024, 58 pages). Programme content: 2023 non-tax revenue 18.7% above budget mainly from CBI proceeds and 2024 revenue 22.6% below the approved estimates mainly from lower CBI contributions (no CBI amounts; these percentages are about total revenue, not CBI, so not recorded); CIU restructured into a statutory body (1 October 2024; already an event from this source) with claims of increased applications and record revenue (no figures); milestones including a ten-week target for application decisions and a 24-hour response time (recorded as an event; the ten weeks are not recorded under processing_time_months, which is in months); SISC and Public Benefit Option described, real-estate thresholds reduced (no amounts); two CBI dividends paid; programme claimed to rank first in the world in 2024 (industry ranking, out of scope). The rest is out of scope.

2026 Budget Address (16 Dec 2025, 53 pages). Programme content: 2025 non-tax revenue 48.3% below budget because of a CBI slowdown, and 2025 total revenue projected about 31.3% below the approved estimates largely because of CBI shortfall (already an event from this source; percentages are about total or non-tax revenue, not recorded); budgetary support to the Nevis Island Administration despite lower CBI revenue; CIU section (paras 48-50): blockchain-verified due diligence certification, Saturn digital platform, role in setting up the Eastern Caribbean CBI Regulatory Authority (new event), top of the CBI Index for a fifth year and awards (industry rankings, out of scope), an Investment Gateway Summit with close to 200 citizens and investors (out of scope), a CIU Micro and Small Business Grant Programme of EC$10,000 each to 36 businesses (in the event description; no total printed, so no observation). No CBI revenue amount is printed. The rest is out of scope.

Revenue table R.08 (p. 107) items 54-15, 54-34, 54-35, 54-36 HRF, 54-37 SGF and, new, 54-40 Sustainable Island State Contribution (2024-2026), recorded as components; the 2024 planned components add to the printed subtotal 545,000 thousand, EC$5 million more than the 2024 CBI estimate on the financial summary (540,000,000), noted in the rows. CIU programme 05041 (pp. 33-34): 2024 appropriation (compensation 1,991, goods and services 72,044, total 74,035) and Main Estimates 2023 (73,945). Out of scope: all other revenue and expenditure lines; 'Fees - Certificate of Citizenship' (ordinary naturalisation) and passport fees; item 61-41 'Hurricane Relief Fund' under the Public Works/Housing (later Agriculture) revenue, which predates and is not the CBI Hurricane Relief Fund contribution; item 61-61 'Investment Proceeds' (not labelled as CBI); the salary-scale annex, which lists the posts of Director of the Citizenship by Investment Unit and Operations Manager, CIU, with general grade salaries. The year-on-year 'Increase/(Decrease)' column is not recorded (a difference of two recorded figures).

SKNIS relay of a Prime Minister's Office statement (6 June 2023): Canada partially lifts the visa requirement imposed on St Kitts and Nevis nationals in 2014; those who held a Canadian visa in the past ten years or hold a current US non-immigrant visa can apply for an eTA; others still need a visa. Already recorded as a visa_access event from this source; no numbers about the programme (the ten-year look-back is a condition, not a statistic).
